paper_title: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Abusive Language Detection in Low-Resource   Settings
caption: : Task-wise Class Distributions
model_annotation: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of classes across different tasks within a benchmark for abusive language detection. The chart comprises thirteen slices, representing categories such as “TIALD”, “Not Abusive”, “Religious”, “Political”, “Abusive”, “Sexist”, “Racist”, “Negative”, “Positive”, “Neutral”, “Mixed”, and “Other”. The slices vary in color, including shades of blue, green, yellow, orange, and pink. Approximate proportions, estimated visually, are as follows: “TIALD” occupies roughly 12% of the chart, “Not Abusive” around 10%, “Religious” about 9%, “Political” around 7%, “Abusive” approximately 7%, “Sexist” about 6%, “Racist” approximately 5%, “Negative” accounts for around 18%, “Positive” approximately 8%, “Neutral” around 8%, “Mixed” covers approximately 12%, and “Other” is approximately 7%. A legend is present in the upper-right corner, identifying each category with a corresponding color, and percentage labels are not displayed directly on the slices. The segments appear to be ordered in a clockwise direction, roughly based on the visual impression of descending segment size.
